en hønsegård.explanation: "En hønsegård" means "a chicken yard". It is built from "høns" (chickens) and "en gård" (a yard). The word "gård" also means "a farm": "Vi bor på en gård" (We live on a farm).

en høring.explanation: "En høring" means "a hearing". It comes from the verb "at høre" (to hear). A very common phrase is "at sende i høring" (to send out for comment): "Loven er sendt i høring" (The law has been sent out for comment).

en høst.explanation: "En høst" means "a harvest". It is the noun for the verb "at høste" (to harvest). To say farmers gather the crop, use the verb: "Bønderne høster kornet" (The farmers harvest the grain).

en høvding.explanation: "En høvding" means "a chieftain". The word is also part of "en indianerhøvding" (a Native American chief).

et halvår.explanation: "Et halvår" means "a half year". It is built from "halv" (half) and "et år" (a year). To talk about one half of the calendar year, use "første halvår" (the first half of the year).

et handicap.explanation: "Et handicap" means "a disability". The form "handicappet" also means "disabled": "Han er handicappet" (He is disabled). When it means "the disability", it is a noun: "Handicappet gør hverdagen svær" (The disability makes everyday life hard).

et hashtag.explanation: "Et hashtag" means "a hashtag". To talk about more than one, add "s": "Hun bruger mange hashtags" (She uses many hashtags).

et hav.explanation: "Et hav" means "a sea". The word also ends the names of oceans, such as "Atlanterhavet" (the Atlantic Ocean). To say where you live, use "ved" (by): "Vi bor ved havet" (We live by the sea). The plural "have" is spelled like "en have" (a garden): "Vi sidder i haven" (We sit in the garden).

et havnebad.explanation: "Et havnebad" means "a harbor bath (outdoor pool)". It is built from "en havn" (a harbor) and "et bad" (a bath). One well-known harbor bath is Havnebadet Islands Brygge in Copenhagen.

et headset.explanation: "Et headset" means "a headset". To say you put it on, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Tag dit headset på" (Put your headset on). The plural has no ending: "to headset" (two headsets).

et hegn.explanation: "Et hegn" means "a fence". Do not mix it up with "en hæk" (a hedge): "Vi har en hæk i stedet for et hegn" (We have a hedge instead of a fence).

et hensyn.explanation: "Et hensyn" means "a consideration". A very common phrase is "at tage hensyn til" (to take into account): "Hun tager altid hensyn til børnene" (She always considers the children).

et hindbær.explanation: "Et hindbær" means "a raspberry". The ending "bær" means "berry", as in "et tranebær" (a cranberry) and "et stikkelsbær" (a gooseberry).

et hit.explanation: "Et hit" means "a hit". It is not used for hitting with your hand. To say someone hits a ball, use "at slå" (to hit): "Han slår bolden" (He hits the ball).

et hjem.explanation: "Et hjem" means "a home". To say you are at home, use "hjemme": "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home). To say you are going home, use "hjem": "Jeg går hjem" (I am going home). Do not mix it up with "et hus" (a house): "Vi har købt et hus" (We have bought a house).

et hjemland.explanation: "Et hjemland" means "a home country". It is built from "hjem" (home) and "et land" (a country). To say you go back there, use "at vende tilbage til" (to return to): "Hun vender tilbage til sit hjemland" (She returns to her home country).

et hjerte.explanation: "Et hjerte" means "a heart". In "hjerte", the "h" is silent, so the word starts with the sound of "y" in "yes". To say you mean something deeply, use: "med hele mit hjerte" (with all my heart).

et hjerteanfald.explanation: "Et hjerteanfald" means "a heart attack". In Denmark, you call 112 in an emergency: "Ring 112!" (Call 112!) Do not mix it up with "et hjertestop" (cardiac arrest): "Ved hjertestop holder hjertet op med at slå" (In a cardiac arrest, the heart stops beating).

et hjerteslag.explanation: "Et hjerteslag" means "a heartbeat". It is built from "et hjerte" (a heart) and "et slag" (a beat). To say how many beats you have in a minute, use "en puls" (a pulse): "Min puls er sytti" (My pulse is seventy).

et hjertestop.explanation: "Et hjertestop" means "a cardiac arrest". It is built from "et hjerte" (a heart) and "et stop" (a stop). To say someone has one, use "at få" (to get): "Manden fik hjertestop" (The man had a cardiac arrest). Do not mix it up with "et hjerteanfald" (a heart attack): "Han fik et hjerteanfald" (He had a heart attack).

et hjul.explanation: "Et hjul" means "a wheel". The word also builds "et cykelhjul" (a bicycle wheel). The plural has no ending: "to hjul" (two wheels).

et hjørne.explanation: "Et hjørne" means "a corner". To say where a shop is on the street, use "på hjørnet" (on the corner): "Bageren ligger på hjørnet" (The bakery is on the corner). To say where something is in a room, use "i hjørnet" (in the corner): "Stolen står i hjørnet" (The chair is in the corner).

et hjørnespark.explanation: "Et hjørnespark" means "a corner kick". It is built from "et hjørne" (a corner) and "et spark" (a kick). The part "spark" also builds "et straffespark" (a penalty kick).

et hobbyrum.explanation: "Et hobbyrum" means "a hobby room". It is built from "en hobby" (a hobby) and "et rum" (a room). The part "rum" also builds "et lagerrum" (a storage room).

et hold.explanation: "Et hold" means "a team". To say people work well together, use it for the group: "Vi er et godt hold" (We are a good team). When you sign up for lessons, it also means "a course group": "Jeg går på et hold om aftenen" (I take a course in the evening).
